assumptions: The initial offer is a secure-upload workflow with manual onboarding and contracted expert review, without laboratory integration, exclusivity, or committed referrals.
Hotel operators already buy laboratory, competent-expert, and facility-management services, so the casebook must earn a separate budget or become part of one of those existing contracts.

The stated 65000 PLN and roughly three founder hours per day are sufficient for a bounded pilot, but not evidence that sales, support, expert governance, and liability management can scale within those constraints.
Planning-stage unknowns are treated as uncertainty rather than failed validation; no pricing, renewal, margin, data rights, partner commitment, or benchmark advantage is assumed.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid multi-site hotel pilot should demonstrate the frequency of qualifying cases, willingness to pay beyond existing lab and consultant services, time-to-close, full contribution margin after expert review, support, insurance and channel costs, repeat use or annual renewal, and a measurable workflow or audit advantage over incumbent portals. A committed distribution partner, explicit reusable-data rights, and enough comparable intervention-to-retest records to produce valid improvements would materially strengthen the channel and defensibility case.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The proposal identifies a concrete gap between an accredited positive result and a governed, documented intervention-to-retest record. Narrowing the product to the operator-owned case file and preserving expert authority is thoughtful, although incumbent non-compliance tools may already cover much of the workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A confirmed exceedance creates urgent health, compliance, reputational, and coordination pain, and official exceedance data show the trigger is real. Separate willingness to pay is nevertheless unproven because laboratories, consultants, and facility systems may already coordinate or document remediation.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-case fees plus a portfolio subscription provide two plausible revenue mechanisms and the pilot capital is bounded. However, price, case frequency, renewal, CAC, expert workload, insurance, support burden, gross margin, payback, and owner earnings are all unknown; episodic cases and required expert involvement could produce weak operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Multi-site hotels are a coherent initial segment with repeated systems, centralized oversight, and visible exposure to Legionella incidents. The economically reachable beachhead is not established, because qualifying positive-to-retest cases may be infrequent and the supplied testing statistics do not show the number of addressable hotel portfolios or their spend.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: An operator-owned system of record could occupy a useful coordination point, but there is no exclusive access, committed channel, proprietary workflow standard, or demonstrated reason it can dominate. Laboratories, consultants, specialist platforms, and facility software are well placed to bundle the same feature around existing customer relationships.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful hotel workflow could extend to healthcare, care, residential, leisure, and other priority premises, and potentially to adjacent water-safety evidence workflows. Expansion is plausible but would add segment-specific expert, regulatory, and system-context requirements and is not yet made easier by a proven asset.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Consented records linking context, signed interventions, and accredited retests could eventually improve templates and create switching value. That moat is conditional on data rights, volume, comparability, and demonstrated predictive usefulness, while the basic case-management workflow is readily copied by incumbents.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A single audit-ready dossier and explicit expert governance may improve convenience, traceability, and accountability compared with fragmented files. The packet provides no measured improvement in response time, compliance effort, remediation success, audit outcomes, or cost, and competing products already advertise trends and non-compliance management.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Regulatory attention, frequent exceedances, and rising reported disease burden support sustained demand for better control workflows. This is favorable momentum, though the obligation and vendor category are established rather than a uniquely open regulatory window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A direct secure-upload pilot avoids a long integration cycle and one multi-site operator could yield several sites. Acquisition still depends on direct enterprise selling or uncommitted introductions from actors able to offer the workflow themselves, and the positive-result trigger makes prospect timing irregular and potentially expensive.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The software and bounded pilot fit the founder's analytical skills, part-time availability, and capital, while outsourcing qualified judgment correctly limits scope. Material execution burdens remain in expert contracting, urgent escalation, secure data handling, liability boundaries, insurance, manual data quality, enterprise sales, and maintaining trust without implying clinical or regulatory authority.

highest_value_structural_change: Make a competent water-safety consultancy or an accredited laboratory the contracted channel and commercial customer for a white-label, operator-owned casebook, with an annual portfolio minimum plus usage fees rather than relying mainly on separately sold positive-case activations. A committed partner would align acquisition with the test result, embed qualified governance, and reduce event-frequency and direct-sales fragility while preserving operator consent for any reusable data.
main_structural_strength: The opportunity is anchored to a narrow, high-stakes operational trigger and deliberately separates workflow software from accredited testing and competent expert decisions, enabling a low-integration pilot that fits the founder's technical strengths and limited initial capital.
primary_score_limiter: The model has no demonstrated source of attractive recurring economics: qualifying events may be sparse, operators may not pay separately, expert and support costs may absorb the case fee, and incumbent labs or platforms can bundle the same workflow through stronger channels.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing laboratory portals and Legionella platforms already offer trend analytics, dashboards, and non-compliance management, while qualified consultants and laboratories sit closest to both the triggering result and remediation process; this directly weakens claimed differentiation, referral leverage, and separate willingness to pay.
